item.title: Lecture 1: Optimization Basics and Existence of Solutions
item.description: Defines optimization problems and key concepts (global/local minima, stationary points), and gives conditions—via lower semicontinuity, compactness, or coercivity—under which minimizers exist, with implications for statistical estimation and algorithms.

item.title: Lecture 2: Convexity, Geometry, and Differentiability in Optimization
item.description: Introduces convex sets and functions, their geometric interpretation via level sets, and fundamental differentiability concepts (Fréchet and directional derivatives), highlighting their role in understanding optimization structure and behavior.

item.title: Lecture 3: Gradient Geometry and Iterative Optimization
item.description: Explains the geometric role of gradients as directions of steepest ascent/descent, their relation to level sets, and motivates iterative optimization via local linear approximations and descent methods.
